key_insight: DreamLite demonstrates that a compact (0.39B) unified diffusion model can run on-device and support both text-to-image generation and text-guided image editing without separate heavy models, achieving a practical tradeoff between capability and efficiency.
problem_solved: Large diffusion models enable high-quality generation and editing but are too big and slow for on-device use; existing lightweight on-device models focus mainly on T2I and lack integrated editing support.
method: Design a unified, lightweight diffusion backbone (0.39B parameters) that shares weights across generation and editing tasks to reduce redundancy and memory footprint.
Introduce efficiency techniques (distillation/parameter-sharing, attention and compute optimizations, and low-bit or quantized runtime) to meet on-device latency and resource constraints.
Train the model with multi-task conditioning (text + optional image/mask references) and joint losses so a single model handles both text-to-image synthesis and text-guided image editing workflows.
impact: Enables low-latency, privacy-friendly image generation and editing on edge devices, lowering deployment cost and broadening access to creative AI tools for mobile/embedded applications.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: compact unified diffusion backbone showing shared weights and task-conditioned inputs (text, image, mask).
Size vs. capability chart: model size/latency comparison (DreamLite 0.39B) against typical multi-billion-parameter diffusion models.
Pipeline illustration: two side-by-side flows for (A) text-to-image generation and (B) text-guided image editing (before/after example).
Performance/efficiency icon set: latency, memory, and on-device deployment badges (e.g., CPU/GPU/mobile compatibility).
paper_title: DreamLite: A Lightweight On-Device Unified Model for Image Generation and Editing
paper_authors: Kailai Feng, Yuxiang Wei, Bo Chen, Yang Pan, Hu Ye
